observations: The upper passage belongs to the broad diagonally cancelled block seen in the whole-page layout.
The long low word after groupes has a late descender and raised marks; envisagés is retained as a doubtful complete reading rather than an expanded abbreviation.
A hooked interlinear insertion above the right end reads fixés par rho, following a locally struck word provisionally read stables. The strike hides letters of that word.
The relative insertion anchor is near the end of envisagés and before il. No additional punctuation is supplied.
All equation signs and indices are visible. The deletion state comes from the encompassing diagonal cancellation in the whole-page layout; no individual horizontal strike crosses this isolated crop.
The diagonal cancellation crosses the beginning of en. The comma between the two indexed letters is visible.
The complete nine-factor equation and all three lower labels are included within the broad cancelled block.
A separate short slant above and right of the initial l_1 could be a prime or an incidental stroke; the local alternative preserves this uncertainty.

The first lower label has a local horizontal deletion and a hooked replacement above it. The replacement is provisionally l_1 sigma_infinity; the diagonal cancellation and local correction overlap its initial letters.
The locally struck label is provisionally l_1^-1 l_infinity^-1 sigma_0 and remains a whole-label doubt.
The second label is l_infinity^-1 l_0^-1; the third is l_0^-1 l_1^-1. No algebraic normalization was used.
The right marginal equation has three separate minus-one exponents.
The short word below the equation has a round initial capital and a second tall joined letter; OK is preferred, with Oh retained as an alternative.
No broad cancellation stroke passes through this marginal note itself.
The rectangular frame is present around the equation and crossed by a diagonal cancellation.
A small dark check-like tick lies below and left of On a, on a faint diagonal line. Its status is uncertain and it is recorded separately from the words.
The broad diagonal cancellation crosses the phrase in several places. The letters of the recovered prose remain visible.
The final indexed sigma is at the right crop edge; its body, index stroke and dot are visible.
All three minus-one exponents are explicit. The first epsilon and final sigma index are retraced but identifiable.
Broad cancellation strokes pass through the left-hand symbols and the final equality area.
The prose reads donc on a la relation inattendue; the three displayed sigma indices are infinity, one and zero.

The long broad cancellation descends through the prose area and stops just above or beside the displayed product. Its scope at this boundary is uncertain. Cancelled and live states are both retained; no mathematical inference settles it.
The first epsilon is heavily retraced but its body and zero index are visible. No cancellation crosses this later statement. No final stop is supplied.
The final subscript in the first row is a dark retraced upright group, provisionally 1; that local doubt remains.
The remaining zero, one and infinity indices and all three negative-one exponents are independently visible.
Two separate horizontal strokes form a separator. The right stroke is approximately three times the length of the left; neither is an equals sign. The TeX rules represent these strokes, not words.
The first line begins with capital Critique and has a definite stop after approche, followed by capital Les.
Two small low marks occur beneath the end of notations. They resemble a colon, but their punctuation status remains uncertain.
The list contains l_i, sigma_i, epsilon_i and rho. Three following ellipsis marks are present, with the last elongated.
Incidental tops of the following line appear at the lower edge and are excluded.
The comma after discrets and the single separate dash before de plus are visible.
Some descenders of groupes and profinis meet the lower crop edge; no continuation beyond the final faudrait is supplied.
The adjective after groupes appears to end with t, with no separate final s recovered; discret is preserved.
The horizontal strike through utiliser obscures some of its small letters, so the whole cancelled word remains doubtful.
The following compact capitalized notation has an open rounded first letter and joined low letters; Aut, Out and Cat remain competing readings.
The two-line sign after that notation has a nearly straight upper stroke and a more wavy lower stroke. Its precise form is unresolved; no mathematical meaning is imposed.
The box ends after pour les, with no supplied continuation.
Both digits are clear. The black scan border is not part of the inscription.
